newsitem.title: USA: NABI says HIV-IG trial enrollment ended.
newsitem.headline: NABI says HIV-IG trial enrollment ended.

text.p: NABI said Wednesday the Data Safety Monitoring Board recommended that the National Institutes of Health discontinue patient enrollment in its Phase III clinical trial of HIV-IG because of an unexpectedly low rate of infant infection.

NABI said the decision was made because current therapy using AZT has reduced the rate of mother to baby HIV transmission so low that it is not feasible to show statistically significant efficacy for a combination of AZT and HIV-IG.

"We share the NIH's gratification that the prospects for babies of HIV- infected mothers have improved so dramatically," said NABI president and chief executive David Gury. "Moreover, HIV-IG may still play a role in HIV therapy, and we plan to continue our Phase II dosing study to test the product's safety and efficacy in the treatment of HIV-infected children."
NABI said the NIH-sponsored pediatric study of HIV-IG is fully enrolled, and completion is expected during 1997.
